front: Antibiotic Stewardship • The 5 Ds: $ Drug (right drug for the right bug) $ Dosing (optimal) $ Drug route $ Duration (suitable) $ De-escalation (timely to pathogen-directed therapy) Susceptibility does not equal sensitivity due to resistance!

Rule 1: NEVER Give a First-Generation Cephalosporin if The reaction to penicillin was anaphylaxis or hives! Immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated, type I hypersensitivity reaction: Each reaction progressively worsens.

Rule 2: Cautious Use of Second- or Third-Generation Cephalosporin if • Type 1 hypersensitivity to PCN • Later generations have dissimilar chemical side chains. ➔ Less potential for cross-reactivity • Less potential for cross-reactivity if >10 years since allergic reaction to penicillin
Rule 3: Give Any Cephalosporin if NOTES • The reaction to penicillin was a morbilliform rash. • Maculopapular drug eruption; usually T cell mediated (type IV hypersensitivity)
